article.articleHeadline: Delhi Battles H1N1 Wave | 1,777 Cases, Naddda Reviews Preparedness | Swine Flu News
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 1,777 H1N1 (swine flu) cases in 2026, making H1N1 the dominant influenza strain in the capital’s current surge. The outbreak has prompted a focus on hospital preparedness, testing, surveillance, and public awareness. Union Health Minister JP Nadda has reviewed the H1N1 situation, directing authorities to strengthen healthcare readiness and measures to manage rising influenza cases. Doctors describe flu-like symptoms including fever, cough, sore throat, body aches and fatigue. High-risk groups—young children, older adults, pregnant women, and people with weakened immunity or underlying conditions—face greater risk of complications. Health officials are urging residents to maintain respiratory hygiene and seek medical advice if symptoms worsen. The report emphasizes Delhi’s ongoing response and preparedness efforts amid the swine flu wave.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1感染拡大、1,777例確認 ナッダ保健相が対策を確認 | 豚インフルエンザ最新情報
triage.triage_reason: デリーでのH1N1感染急増（1,777例）に対し保健相が直接対応状況を確認するなど政府・社会的関心が高く、ヒト-ヒト感染や継続的曝露のリスクがあるためWPRO基準を満たす。
triage.notes: H1N1は季節性インフルエンザとして既知の病原体であり、IHR基準上は異常性・国際拡大リスクは低いが、感染者数の急増と政府の積極的対応から社会的関心が高く、続報の確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Rientra da un viaggio in Congo e ha i sintomi sospetti dell'Ebola: un uomo in isolamento in Trentino
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Man returns from a trip to Congo with Ebola-suspected symptoms, in isolation in Trentino.
article.articleSummary: As of 22 August 2026, a man who recently returned from the Democratic Republic of the Congo is in home isolation in Trentino on suspicion of Ebola. He developed symptoms compatible with the virus, and Italian authorities activated the Ministry of Health–mandated procedures; he is considered low risk and his samples have been sent to Luigi Sacco Hospital in Milan for definitive confirmation. The protocol does not confirm infection and emphasizes that Ebola transmission requires direct contact with blood, secretions, or other bodily fluids of an infected person. The Congolese outbreak continues to worsen: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) reports it is the largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic in the country’s history, with about one death every thirty minutes, and spreading amid conflict, displacement, hunger, and other health emergencies.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ旅行から帰国した男性、エボラ疑い症状でトレンティーノにて隔離
triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ流行はMSFにより「同国史上最大・最悪」と報告されており、既に渡航者を通じた疑い例がイタリアで発生するなど国際的拡大の兆候がある。IHR基準複数該当のためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はイタリア国内での疑い例だが、背景として言及されているDRCのエボラ流行が『史上最大・最悪』とされ、実質的な発生国はDRCである。イタリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Congo receives more than 16,000 doses of Ebola vaccine as it grapples with unprecedented outbreak
article.articleSummary: Congo receives 16,250 doses of Ervebo Ebola vaccine at Kinshasa's N'djili airport, part of 70,000 doses from WHO and partners with more due early next week, as the country fights an unprecedented Bundibugyo-virus outbreak. The outbreak has 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths as of Friday; symptoms can resemble malaria, and there is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo, though Ervebo may offer some protection against it. Transmission is accelerating and not yet peaked, with projections that it could triple. The Ebola vaccination effort, while bolstering response, faces significant containment challenges, including armed conflict that disrupts control in hotspot cities, attacks on medical personnel and facilities, a mobile and displaced population, and inadequate infrastructure.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ、前例のないエボラ流行に対応するため1万6000回分以上のワクチンを受領
triage.triage_reason: DRCで前例のない規模のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が発生し、感染者5,290人・死者2,516人、感染拡大が続き武力紛争で対応が困難な状況であり、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株には承認された治療法・ワクチンがなく、既存のエボラワクチン(Ervebo)による部分的防御効果が期待される段階。武力紛争、医療従事者への攻撃、住民の移動性の高さが封じ込めを困難にしている。

article.articleHeadline: 史上最凶猛伊波拉蔓延！民主剛果逾6成死者「倒在治療中心外」
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The fiercest Ebola outbreak in history! Over 60% of deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo occurred outside treatment centers.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is accelerating at a historically rapid pace. As of August 16, 2026, WHO reports 5,021 confirmed cases and 2,378 deaths. Doctors Without Borders (MSF) notes that more than 60% of fatalities have occurred outside Ebola treatment centers, with many deaths occurring far from care and ongoing community transmission. MSF has treated over 2,000 patients, of which more than 800 are laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases; in the past week, roughly one Ebola death every half hour has been recorded. Trish Newport, MSF Ituri province emergency project manager, urged rapid deployment of trained healthcare workers to treatment centers and intensified community outreach for early case finding, safe patient transfer, and strengthened infection prevention and control. UN/WHO leaders warn the outbreak is spreading at unprecedented speed and requires a broader, community-driven response. Taiwan extended its border controls with the DRC by 90 days to Nov 28; Uganda’s restrictions may be lifted if no new cases.

triage.headline_ja: 史上最凶猛エボラ蔓延！民主コンゴで死者の6割超が「治療センター外で死亡」
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱が過去最速のペースで拡大し、確定症例5,021人・死者2,378人と大規模化しており、国際的拡大・渡航制限（台湾・ウガンダの国境措置）も発生しているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・台湾は国境管理措置の対象として言及されているが、感染発生国はDRCのみ。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: डीआरसी में इबोला तेजी से फैल रहा संक्रमण, मृतकों की संख्या 2,500 के पार | Beni: Ebola outbreak in Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola is a rapidly spreading infection in the DRC; the death toll has crossed 2,500 | Beni: Ebola outbreak in Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is accelerating. As of 21 August 2026, Africa CDC reports 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths, with authorities warning the true burden is higher since only about 30-40% of cases are detected. The epidemic is driven by Bundibugyo virus; there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment. Symptoms may be milder than other Ebola strains, delaying hospital or public-health engagement. Ongoing armed conflict, large-scale displacement, and continuous population movement in eastern DRC complicate control efforts. Transmission has reached six provinces across 56 health zones, with Bas-Uele reporting two new cases recently. Case finding among contacts is weak: fewer than 10% of new cases are among individuals under surveillance, far below the 90–95% target for containment. About 97% of deaths occurred outside hospitals as of 17 August. If unchecked, this surge could surpass the 2014-16 West Africa outbreak (over 28,000 cases, more than 11,000 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: DRCでエボラ出血熱が急速に拡大、死者数が2,500人を超える｜ベニ：コンゴでエボラ流行
triage.triage_reason: IHR4基準中複数該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常事態、国際的拡大リスク）に加え、武装紛争下での制御困難、低い接触者追跡率など制御可能性への懸念が大きく、フルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: Africa CDC報告によれば確認症例5,290件、死亡2,516人（2026年8月21日時点）。実際の症例数は検出率30-40%とされるためさらに多いと推定。ブンディブギョウイルス株によるもので承認済みワクチン・特異的治療法がなく、症状が軽いため医療機関受診が遅れる傾向。武装紛争・大規模な人口移動により制御が困難で、接触者追跡率は目標(90-95%)を大きく下回る10%未満。2014-16年西アフリカ流行を超える恐れがあると指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, negativo test effettuato su caso sospetto emerso in Trentino
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, negative test performed on a suspected case that emerged in Trentino.
article.articleSummary: Ebola suspected in Trentino, Italy. Samples collected from a traveler returning from the Democratic Republic of the Congo were tested at Milan's Sacco Hospital and returned negative. After an initial alarm, authorities confirmed no Ebola positivity. The symptomatic patient prompted testing, with laboratory confirmation ruling out infection. The Ministry of Health, through the Department of Prevention, remains in contact with local authorities and continues to monitor the evolving situation. No confirmed cases or deaths are reported, and surveillance remains in place for potential imported cases. The case underscores ongoing vigilance against Ebola, with coordinated public health oversight across regional health units in Italy.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ、トレンティーノで発生した疑い症例の検査結果は陰性
triage.triage_reason: イタリアの疑い症例は検査の結果陰性が確認されており、対象国での実際の感染事例ではないため見送りと判断。

article.articleHeadline: CDC AS Wanti-wanti Virus Zika di Bali, Ini Gejala yang Perlu Diwaspadai
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: U.S. CDC Warns About Zika Virus in Bali, Here Are the Symptoms to Watch Out For.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-22, the U.S. CDC issued a Level 2 Travel Health Notice for Zika in Bali, Indonesia, after rising reports of Zika among travelers returning from Bali. Zika is a mosquito-borne virus found in tropical and subtropical regions across Africa, the Americas, South Asia, and the Western Pacific. Most infections are asymptomatic or mild; common symptoms include fever, rash, headache, joint and muscle pain, and red eyes, lasting several days to about a week. The illness can resemble dengue or chikungunya. While typically mild, Zika poses serious risks during pregnancy, including birth defects, miscarriage, fetal death, stillbirth, and preterm birth. Rare cases may trigger Guillain-Barré syndrome; even more rarely, neurological complications such as encephalitis, meningitis, or myelitis with bleeding or clotting abnormalities. Travelers from Bali should consider exposure history in clinical assessments.

triage.headline_ja: 米CDC、バリ島のジカウイルスに警告 ― 注意すべき症状とは
triage.triage_reason: 米CDCがバリ島に対しジカウイルスのレベル2渡航健康通知を発出しており、渡航制限リスクと妊婦への深刻な健康影響が確認されるためIHR基準を2つ満たす。
triage.notes: ジカウイルス自体は既知の蚊媒介感染症であり、バリ島からの帰国者間での報告増加を受けて米CDCが渡航健康通知を発出した事例。米国・スペインなど他地域は帰国者の発症地であり、発生地としては対象外。

article.articleHeadline: Kemenkes masifkan deteksi dini TB lewat CKG di 508 lokasi Sulteng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health ramps up early detection of TB through CKG in 508 locations across Central Sulawesi.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia’s Ministry of Health expands early TB detection in Central Sulawesi (Sulawesi Tengah) by launching Free Health Checks (CKG) focused on tuberculosis at 508 sites across 13 regencies/cities, part of a nationwide plan at 53,335 locations. Each session screens 100 people, aiming to accelerate case finding so patients can begin treatment promptly and reduce transmission. The program complements ongoing TB control amid 2025 estimates of 1.09 million TB cases nationwide, with only about 867,000 detected (≈80%). Household contacts will be screened and offered preventive therapy. Sulawesi Tengah’s CKG may involve universities and private sector partners for community education. Operational budget is Rp7.5 million per CKG event, and 16 lightweight (≈3 kg) X-ray units will support on-site detection. Remarks by Deputy Health Minister Benjamin Paulus Octavianus in Palu on 22 August 2026.

article.articleHeadline: स्वाइन फ्लू के मामले दिल्ली में बढ़ रहे हैं, जानिए क्यों होता है और क्या हैं बचने के उपाय
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Swine flu cases are rising in Delhi; learn why it occurs and what preventive measures can be taken.
article.articleSummary: Delhi and other parts of India report rising H1N1 influenza A (swine flu) cases, with Delhi-NCR alone recording over 1,700 confirmed infections this year (PTI). Symptoms mimic seasonal flu—fever, cough, cold, body pains—but can progress to pneumonia, respiratory failure, and death in about 15% of patients, especially those with risk factors. Transmission is mainly via respiratory droplets; surface contamination also spreads the virus. PCR-based testing on throat or nasal swabs provides results within 24 hours, after which patients should isolate. High-risk individuals should start antiviral treatment promptly; severe signs warrant emergency care. At-risk groups include people over 65, diabetics, hypertensives, cardiovascular disease, obesity, pregnant women, and children under five. Annual influenza vaccination remains the best prevention, reducing swine flu risk by 40-50% and lessening severity. Vaccination is advised during Sep-Oct; travelers should consider vaccination even if under 65.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでスワインフルー（H1N1）の症例が増加中：原因と予防策とは
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1インフルエンザの症例が今年1,700件超と増加しているが、季節性・毎年発生する既知の疾患であり、異常性や国際的拡大の兆候は見られないため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 季節性H1N1インフルエンザに関する予防啓発記事であり、デリーでの症例増加を報告しているが、インドでは毎年発生する既知の疾患パターンであるため緊急性は低いと判断。

article.articleHeadline: दिल्ली में H1N1 का बढ़ा खतरा! कितना गंभीर है स्वाइन फ्लू? जानें लक्षण और बचाव
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Delhi, the risk of H1N1 has increased! How serious is swine flu? Learn the symptoms and prevention measures.
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports rising H1N1 influenza A (swine flu) cases during the monsoon, with over 1,300 infections in early August and later reports surpassing 1,400. Most recover, but severe disease is riskier for children under 5 (especially under 2), adults 65+, pregnant women, and those with asthma, diabetes, heart disease, or weakened immunity. Common symptoms include high fever, cough, sore throat, headache, body aches, chills, and fatigue; vomiting or diarrhea can occur in children. Alarm signs—breathing difficulty, low oxygen, chest pain, blue lips/face, or extreme drowsiness/confusion—require urgent care, especially for dehydrated or lethargic children. Prevention includes handwashing, masking in crowded indoors, avoiding close contact with the sick, resting at home, and routine surface cleaning. Lab testing may be advised; vaccination reduces hospitalization for high-risk groups, though it does not guarantee infection prevention. Antibiotics do not treat influenza.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1(豚インフルエンザ)の脅威が拡大！ 重症度と予防法は？
triage.triage_reason: デリーでのH1N1感染者数がモンスーン期に1,400例を超えて増加しており、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性や持続的曝露が懸念されるため、WPRO基準に該当し社会的関心も示唆される。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)のモンスーン期増加であり、例年同様の傾向の可能性があるが、症例数の増加と一般向け注意喚起記事であるため経過観察が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Perluasan Program Wolbachia di Jakarta Barat untuk Tekan Kasus DBD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Expansion of the Wolbachia Program in West Jakarta to Curb Dengue Fever Cases
article.articleSummary: As of August 22, 2026, West Jakarta is expanding a Wolbachia mosquito program to curb dengue fever (DBD). Health authorities are releasing Aedes aegypti mosquitoes infected with Wolbachia bacteria to block dengue virus replication, thereby reducing transmission risk. West Jakarta was selected due to high population density and epidemiological risk, following demonstrations of reduced dengue cases in similar pilots in other Indonesian cities. Deployments involve placing containers with Wolbachia-infected mosquito eggs in residential areas, executed progressively under technical supervision to establish a Wolbachia-dominated vector population that replaces virus-carrying mosquitoes. Community outreach emphasizes safety for people and the environment; residents are asked not to tamper with or discard the educational buckets. The program complements ongoing mosquito-control efforts (PSN). Data on release points and target reductions are still being updated, and residents should maintain good practices (PHBS and 3M Plus) despite the program.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱症例抑制のため西ジャカルタでウォルバキア・プログラムを拡大
triage.triage_reason: 既存の蚊媒介対策プログラムの拡大に関する通常の公衆衛生施策であり、異常な感染急増や新規事象の報告ではないため。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱対策としてのワクチン様媒介動物制御（ウォルバキア菌感染蚊放出）プログラムの拡大に関する報道であり、症例数の急増や異常発生を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Kemendiktisaintek dorong PT dan pemda di Sulteng bersinergi atasi TB
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology urges private sector and local governments in Central Sulawesi to collaborate to tackle tuberculosis.
article.articleSummary: Central Sulawesi faces a sizeable TB burden, with Palu reporting the highest detected cases at 1,075, followed by Parigi Moutong (546) and Banggai (510) in the latest national counts. Seven public and private universities in Sulawesi Tengah—Universitas Tadulako, Universitas Alkhairat, Universitas Tompotika Luwuk, Universitas Muhammadiyah Palu, Universitas Widya Nusantara, Poltekkes, and STIK Indonesia Jaya—are collaborating with health services (RS Untad, Lab Kesda Sulteng) and local governments to tackle TB through research-based, community-oriented approaches. The initiative, led by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology, emphasizes universities' social responsibility and calls for joint action with the private sector and provincial authorities. Officials note gaps in community TB case finding, prompting expanded surveillance and public health measures across Central Sulawesi as of August 22, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 教育・文化・研究・技術省、中スラウェシ州の大学と地方政府に結核対策での連携を促す
triage.triage_reason: 既知の風土病である結核の症例数報告と対策協力に関する行政ニュースであり、突発的・異常な公衆衛生事象ではないため。
triage.notes: 結核は既知の地方流行病であり、記事は大学・行政の対策連携に関する通常業務報告。急性の公衆衛生上の脅威ではない。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases rise in Delhi-NCR amid monsoon, seasonal transition: Doctors
article.articleSummary: H1N1 influenza rising in Delhi-NCR amid monsoon and seasonal transition. Over the past 3–4 weeks, hospitals report a surge in respiratory symptoms, with testing showing a significant uptick in H1N1 cases and doctors noting about 7–10 H1N1 patients daily in OPD, alongside a slight rise in COVID-19. Most H1N1 infections are mild, with fever typically subsiding in 3–5 days. Vulnerable groups—elderly, young children, and those with diabetes, hypertension, heart or kidney disease—face higher risk of complications. Physicians at AIIMS Delhi, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, and Fortis Memorial Research Institute attribute the trend to seasonal monsoon temperature changes that favor influenza, with post-rainy season upticks and more influenza A cases. Symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, nasal discharge, headache, and body aches. Advise isolation at home for 2–3 days, mask-wearing, and prompt medical advice; severe symptoms warrant care.

triage.headline_ja: デリー首都圏でH1N1症例が増加、モンスーンと季節の変わり目が要因―医師ら指摘
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ（H1N1）の例年見られる増加傾向であり、重症化例や異常な広がりの報告はなく、公衆衛生上の緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 季節性のH1N1増加で、大部分が軽症。基礎疾患者や高齢者などのハイリスク群への注意喚起にとどまる内容。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, dopo il caso sospetto in Trentino i risultati delle analisi:
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, after the suspected case in Trentino, the results of the analyses:
article.articleSummary: An adult citizen returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo and displaying Ebola-compatible symptoms prompted a suspected case in Trentino. Tests at Luigi Sacco Hospital in Milan were negative for Ebola, according to the Health Ministry. The person was placed in home isolation, and samples were collected on August 21 and sent to Sacco Hospital for the standard laboratory workup. The negative result followed a precautionary contact-mapping effort by the Prevention Department of the local health authority. Local and national health authorities maintained vigilance, undertaking trace-and-monitor of identified contacts. No further cases have been reported, underscoring that the response was preventive, pending confirmed exclusion of infection.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、トレンティーノでの疑い例後、検査結果は陰性
triage.triage_reason: イタリア・トレンティーノでの疑い例はエボラ検査の結果陰性であり、実際の感染事例は確認されていないため、対象国での発生イベントとしては該当しない。
triage.notes: 疑い例はイタリアで発生し検査は陰性。DRCへの渡航歴はあるが、DRC国内での発生を報じる記事ではないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Point Santé : Ebola franchit le cap des 5000 cas ; mais de bonnes nouvelles sur le front de la polio...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health Update: Ebola surpasses the 5,000-case milestone; but good news on the polio front.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo surpasses 5,000 confirmed cases and 2,325 deaths, the deadliest Bundibugyo outbreak in the DRC. The WHO on August 19 kept the public health emergency of international concern; risk remains very high in DRC and neighboring countries. The response uses motorcycle riders as surveillance/intervention agents, with 100 epidemiologists, 500+ health workers, and about 400 new beds. On August 20, WHO and Africa CDC allocated 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC, including 20,000 for a Phase 3 trial against Bundibugyo and 50,000 for frontline workers; Gavi funds transport and vaccination. Efficacy against Bundibugyo in humans is unproven; two other vaccines (Moderna, Oxford) are in early trials, with Hilleman Laboratories highlighted. Five African countries—Burundi, Ghana, Guinea-Bissau, Uganda, Republic of Congo—have ended outbreaks of vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2. Institut Pasteur launched a continent-wide chikungunya vaccine project. About 60% of the $115 million needed has been mobilized.

triage.headline_ja: 健康速報：エボラが5,000症例を突破、しかしポリオ対策では朗報
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱がWHOによりPHEIC継続中で5,000例・2,325人死亡と深刻化しており、IHR基準の複数項目に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 主要な事象はDRCでのエボラ（ブンディブジョ株）流行拡大とWHOのPHEIC継続。ガーナは過去のワクチン由来ポリオ発生終息の報告として言及されており、現在進行中の発生ではない。ウガンダ・ブルンジ・ギニアビサウ・コンゴ共和国は対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 埃博拉已夺2516人命　逾1.6万剂疫苗运抵刚果（金）
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has claimed 2,516 lives; over 16,000 doses of vaccine have arrived in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 22 August 2026, DR Congo’s 17th Ebola outbreak, declared 15 May, has 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths. A batch of 16,250 Ervebo vaccine doses arrived at Kinshasa airport on Friday, part of a WHO-arranged total of 70,000 doses: 20,000 for clinical trials and 50,000 for frontline health workers. Ervebo protects against Zaire ebolavirus, not Bundibugyo; cross-protection remains uncertain though early data, including animal studies, suggest possible benefit. UN Ebola Emergency Response Coordinator warns the outbreak is expanding exponentially. Ervebo has been deployed before, notably during 2018–2020 outbreaks. Separately, two Bundibugyo-targeting vaccines are in clinical trials—Moderna (mRNA) and Oxford University—with a third candidate, rVSV Bundibugyo, under development by Hilleman Laboratories in Singapore. Ebola spreads via contact with bodily fluids and has killed more than 15,000 in Africa over the past five decades.

triage.headline_ja: エボラで2,516人死亡　1.6万回分以上のワクチンがコンゴ民主共和国に到着
triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模エボラアウトブレイク（確定5,290例、死亡2,516例）が指数関数的に拡大中とUNが警告しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: この株はBundibugyoエボラウイルスであり、既存のErveboワクチン（Zaire株対象）の交差防御効果は不確実。致死率が高く（約47.6%）、UNは指数関数的拡大を警告しており、国際的な支援・ワクチン投入が進行中。Singaporeは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Negativo al test per l'Ebola il caso sospetto in Trentino - Medicina
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola test negative for suspected case in Trentino - Medicine
article.articleSummary: As of 22 August 2026, Ebola testing of samples from a person returning from the Democratic Republic of the Congo was negative. The individual, from Trentino, had presented with symptoms and was subjected to testing at Milan’s Sacco Hospital, with results reported by the Italian Ministry of Health. The note indicates the patient was treated as a suspected Ebola case and tested accordingly; the negative result means no infection was confirmed. The case is characterized as imported from the DRC, and authorities did not report additional details on contacts or follow-up in the published statement. The outcome emphasizes ongoing vigilance for hemorrhagic fever symptoms in travelers from high‑risk regions, but there is currently no evidence of an active Ebola outbreak linked to this incident.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ検査は陰性、トレンティーノの疑い症例 - 医療
triage.triage_reason: イタリア・トレンティーノでの疑い症例はエボラ検査陰性と確定しており、DRCでの発生を示す情報も本記事にはないため、シグナルとして取り上げる根拠がない。
triage.notes: 本記事はイタリアでの疑い例が陰性確定した事例であり、DRCでのエボラ発生自体を報じるものではないため、対象国リストにおけるDRCの実発生は確認できない。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo receives 1st batch of vaccines to contain Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: DR Congo received the first batch of 16,520 Ervebo Ebola vaccine doses to contain the outbreak, with authorities expecting more than 50,000 additional doses by Monday. The World Health Organization announced 70,000 vaccines would be supplied for a Phase 3 trial to assess the vaccine’s impact on the Bundibugyo virus and to protect frontline and health workers; no vaccine or specific treatment exists yet for Bundibugyo virus. Ervebo is licensed and recommended for Ebola virus disease outbreaks (formerly Zaire ebolavirus). As of the latest Health Ministry update, confirmed Ebola infections total 5,290 with more than 2,500 deaths. The epidemic has affected 56 health zones across six provinces—Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele and Tshopo—since mid-May. MSF warned that communities lack adequate support, urging intensified training for health workers and community leaders on case detection, referrals, and infection prevention and control measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ流行封じ込めのため第1便のワクチンを受領
triage.triage_reason: 確定感染者5,290人、死者2,500人超と深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、6州56保健圏に拡大する大規模なエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）流行でIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 本流行は通常のザイールエボラウイルスではなくブンディブギョウイルスによるものであり、ワクチン・治療法未確立の点が特に懸念される。MSFはコミュニティ支援の不足を警告しており、国際支援の継続が必要とされる。

article.articleHeadline: Sarawak confirms 26 rabies cases this year, including three cats
article.articleSummary: Rabies in Sarawak, Malaysia: 26 animals tested positive this year (23 dogs, 3 cats) as of 20 Aug 2026 per DVSS. Since July 2017, the state has 94 human rabies cases with 87 deaths (≈93% fatality), underscoring that rabies is almost universally fatal once symptoms appear but entirely preventable. Public health guidance: treat every animal bite or scratch as an emergency; vaccinate pets annually and practice responsible ownership; immediately wash any wound with soap under running water for at least 15 minutes and seek a health clinic. The Stop Rabies 2026: Rabies Education Carnival at Universiti Malaysia Sarawak, supported by MyOHUN and Boehringer Ingelheim (Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia), and involving JKNS, DVSS and SSPCA, aims toward Zero Human Rabies Deaths by 2030. The event awarded Rabies Hero Ambassadors; champions include SMK Jalan Arang (secondary) and SJK(C) Chung Hua Sematan (primary), among others.

triage.headline_ja: サラワク州、今年26件の狂犬病症例を確認、うち猫3件を含む
triage.triage_reason: マレーシア・サラワク州における狂犬病の年次報告であり、対象国リストに該当する国での発生ではなく、地域内の風土病的状況として教育啓発イベントの文脈で報じられているため。
triage.notes: インドネシア・シンガポールは狂犬病教育イベントのスポンサー企業の活動地域として言及されているのみで、実際の狂犬病発生地はマレーシア・サラワク州（対象国リストに含まれず）。狂犬病は同地域で既知の風土病であり、通常の年次報告・啓発活動の一環と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: وصول 16 ألف جرعة لقاح إيرفيبو لمكافحة إيبولا في الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Arrival of 16,000 Ervebo vaccine doses to combat Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) intensifies as the seventh Ebola outbreak, with transmission spanning northern and eastern regions amid weak state presence and limited health infrastructure and ongoing armed-group activity. The government reports 5,290 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths. On Friday, 16,000 Ervebo vaccine doses arrived at N'djili airport in Kinshasa; WHO has pledged a total of 70,000 doses for DRC, with 20,000 for clinical trials and 50,000 for frontline health workers. Ervebo targets Zaire ebolavirus, but its efficacy against Bundibugyo ebolavirus currently circulating is unconfirmed; early animal data suggest possible protection. The vaccine has been used previously, notably between 2018 and 2020. UN Ebola response coordinator Julian Harnis warns the outbreak is accelerating.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ対策のためエルベボワクチン1万6千回分が到着
triage.triage_reason: DRCで第7次エボラ流行が拡大し、確認症例5,290件・死亡2,516件と深刻な公衆衛生上の影響があり、国連調整官も流行加速を警告しているためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 現行流行株はBundibugyoエボラウイルスであり、エルベボワクチン（ザイール株対応）の有効性は未確認。武装勢力の活動や医療インフラの脆弱性により感染拡大リスクが高い。

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases rise in Delhi-NCR: Why not every fever patient is being tested, here's what Delhi hospitals' rules say; Know what's happening in Noida, Gurugram, Ghaziabad, Faridabad?
article.articleSummary: Delhi-NCR sees a seasonal influenza rise with H1N1 the dominant influenza-A strain, reporting 2392 influenza-A cases this year, including 1777 H1N1 infections. The government has strengthened surveillance and hospital preparedness; Union Health Minister JP Nadda met officials, and Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh said beds, doctors, medicines and equipment are sufficient. Testing is not universal; guidelines classify patients into: mild symptoms—no test; moderate/high fever or severe throat infection or high-risk conditions—testing considered; severe symptoms (breathing difficulty, chest pain, hypotension, blood in sputum)—RT-PCR and hospitalization. Delays in test results persist; total tests conducted and average turnaround are not publicly disclosed. Surveillance through the Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme and the Delhi State Health Mission includes reinforced screening and hygiene guidance throughout Delhi and the NCR, including Noida, Gurugram, Ghaziabad and Faridabad. Health advisories urge masks in crowded places and prompt medical advice if symptoms worsen.

triage.headline_ja: デリー首都圏でH1N1感染例が増加：なぜすべての発熱患者が検査されないのか、デリーの病院ルールとノイダ・グルガオン・ガジアバード・ファリダバードの状況とは
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザ（H1N1優勢株）の症例増加だが、政府は監視・医療体制を強化中で重症例の急増や国際的拡大の兆候は明確でない。季節性の流行として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザの通常の年次変動である可能性が高く、政府は既存の監視プログラム（IDSP）で対応中。重症度や死亡者数など具体的な臨床アウトカムの情報が不足しているため、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Monsoon viral infections: Dr Guleria advises annual influenza vaccine
article.articleSummary: Influenza vaccination is advised during the monsoon spike in viral infections in India, with high-risk individuals urged to get the annual flu shot, says Dr Randeep Guleria. The former AIIMS Delhi director and current chair of Medanta's Institute of Internal Medicine and Respiratory & Sleep Medicine told ANI that most monsoon illnesses are mild and can be managed with standard home care. The guidance, issued during the monsoon season, emphasizes vaccination as a preventive measure; no specific case/death counts or outbreaks are cited in the article. No laboratory-confirmed outbreak details are provided. Guleria specifically highlighted that older adults, people with chronic illnesses, and frontline workers should prioritize vaccination, aligning with public health measures for seasonal influenza protection. Publication date: 2026-08-22.

triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザに関する予防啓発記事であり、具体的な症例数・死亡数・アウトブレイクの報告はなく、公衆衛生上の異常事態を示す情報も含まれていない。
triage.notes: 記事は季節性インフルエンザワクチン接種の推奨に関する一般的な医療アドバイス記事であり、具体的なアウトブレイクや症例報告は含まれていないため、対象国リストへの計上は不適切と判断（発生地域にIndiaが含まれるが、イベントとしての異常性がないため見送り）。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديموقراطية تستقبل أكثر من 16 ألف جرعة من لقاح إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Democratic Republic of the Congo receives more than 16,000 doses of the Ebola vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)—the deadliest in the country’s history—continues as vaccines arrive. The DRC received 16,000 doses of Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) Ebola vaccine, with reports that 16,250 doses were received at N’djili airport. The outbreak, declared May 15 as the seventh Ebola outbreak in the DRC, likely began weeks earlier and is spreading across northern and eastern regions amid weak health infrastructure and ongoing armed conflict. The World Health Organization announced a total of 70,000 Ervebo doses for the DRC, the only vaccine officially approved, manufactured by Merck in Germany. Although Ervebo targets the Zaire ebolavirus lineage, its efficacy against Bundibugyo is unconfirmed; preliminary animal data suggest possible protection. DRC Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba noted the vaccine’s prior use (2018–2020). Of the 70,000 doses, 20,000 are for clinical trials and 50,000 for frontline health workers.

triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最悪とされるエボラ出血熱の流行が継続中であり、武力紛争と脆弱な保健インフラの中で拡大が続いているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ドイツはワクチン製造国（Merck）として記事に登場するのみで、感染発生地ではないためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: المركزية | 16 ألف جرعة من لقاح إيبولا تصل إلى الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 16,000 doses of an Ebola vaccine arrive in Congo.
article.articleSummary: 16,000 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine arrived in the Democratic Republic of the Congo on Friday as the country confronts the deadliest Ebola outbreak in its history. The outbreak, declared on May 15 as the seventeenth in DRC, likely began spreading weeks earlier and continues to affect the northern and eastern regions where state presence is weak and health infrastructure is nearly non-existent amid longstanding armed groups. The World Health Organization announced that DRC will receive 70,000 additional Ervebo doses manufactured in Germany, the only Ebola vaccine with formal approval. Ervebo is confirmed to be effective against the Zaire ebolavirus strain; however, efficacy against Bundibugyo ebolavirus currently circulating is not yet confirmed. Early, animal-based data suggest it may offer some protection against Bundibugyo.

article.articleHeadline: Veteran actor Poonam Dhillon hospitalized due to dengue
article.articleSummary: Dengue confines veteran actor Poonam Dhillon to hospital, admitted to Mumbai's Lilavati Hospital, in a health update published on 2026-08-22. Dhillon, a veteran actress and president of the Cine and TV Artistes Association (CINTAA), was diagnosed with dengue, according to journalist Vickey Lalwani who posted the update on Instagram. Lalwani stated that Dhillon 'has been diagnosed with dengue and has been in the hospital for quite some days now,' and a subsequent message cited by the journalist said she is recovering and hoped to be back home soon. The report provides a hospitalization status for a public figure in Mumbai with dengue, but offers no details on illness severity, laboratory confirmation, or exposure source.

article.articleHeadline: स्वाइन फ्लू को ना करे नजरअंदाज, ख्याल रखें इन बातों का | Do not ignore swine flu; keep these points in mind.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Do not ignore swine flu; keep these points in mind.
article.articleSummary: New Delhi, with changing weather, fever, cough, sore throat, headache and body aches may be mistaken for a common viral illness. These signs can also indicate swine flu, i.e., H1N1 infection. Do not panic; take precautions and consult a doctor if symptoms persist or worsen. For feverish or flu-like symptoms, rest and stay hydrated; avoid rushing back to work. If you must go out, wear a mask and keep a safe distance from others, especially when near the elderly, young children, pregnant women or people with preexisting conditions. Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue, dispose of it properly, and wash hands frequently; use sanitizer if needed. Do not self-treat with antibiotics or antivirals; not every fever is flu. A clinician may order tests and provide treatment based on symptoms and risk factors.

The Ministry of Health's protocol for suspected Ebola was activated in response to the case. The individual was immediately placed in home isolation, and healthcare workers collected samples that were sent to Luigi Sacco for confirmation and analysis. No Ebola infection was confirmed. The episode demonstrates national adherence to Ebola protocols and ongoing surveillance in import-related exposure scenarios.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Special camp to detect elephantiasis among North Indian workers near Tiruchendur.
article.articleSummary: Near Tiruchendur, Tamil Nadu, a midnight blood-collection camp was held in Veerapandiya Pettai to preemptively screen North Indian migrant workers employed at a private star-hotel construction site for elephantiasis (lymphatic filariasis). District Health Officer Dr. Yazhini authorized the drive, with local health oversight. Public health inspector Aristattil and health inspectors Rajesh, Muthuramaran, and Mugil from Kayalpattinam collected blood samples at midnight, when nocturnal microfilariae are most detectable. All samples have been sent to laboratories for analysis; results, once available, will guide medical advice and provision of anti-filarial treatment or preventive measures for those testing positive. The effort aims at early detection and management, ensuring appropriate care for infected individuals and steps to prevent further transmission. Processing continues with laboratory confirmations pending.

article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis remains a major health issue in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. The Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology (Kemendiktisaintek) urges universities across Sulawesi Tengah to strengthen synergy with local governments to tackle TB and related social issues. Seven higher education institutions—Universitas Tadulako, Universitas Alkhairat, Universitas Tompotika Luwuk, Universitas Muhammadiyah Palu, Universitas Widya Nusantara, Poltekkes, and STIK Indonesia Jaya—are collaborating with health service units such as RS Untad, Lab Kesda Sulteng, puskesmas, and local authorities to devise research-based solutions and community service. Central government data show a substantial gap in TB case finding, with Palu reporting 1,075 cases, Parigi Moutong 546, Banggai 510, and other districts below 500. The initiative promotes universities as social entities contributing to public health, amid efforts to address poverty and unemployment through joint research and service.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Concern grows as dengue infections rise during the rainy season; learn which serious symptoms differentiate from a typical fever and require immediate medical help.
article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-22, in New Delhi, concerns grow as dengue infections rise during the rainy season (July–October). Dengue is transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes breeding in stagnant water around homes after rains. Early dengue often resembles a simple viral fever, but major symptoms include high fever, headache, body pains, weakness, nausea, and vomiting. Diagnosis cannot rely on symptoms alone; medical assessment and likely laboratory testing are needed for confirmation. Severe warning signs require urgent care: sudden extreme weakness or dizziness, rapid breathing, persistent severe abdominal pain, nose or gum bleeding, vomiting blood, or blood in stools. Treatment focuses on maintaining fluids, controlling symptoms, and monitoring for complications; avoid self-medicating with aspirin or ibuprofen without doctor’s advice. Prevention includes eliminating standing water, regular cleaning of containers, and using protective clothing and mosquito repellents.

article.articleHeadline: Delhi H1N1 Cases Reach 1,777 Amid Flu Surge
article.articleSummary: Delhi reports 1,777 confirmed H1N1 infections in 2026 amid rising influenza activity, up from 1,449 as of August 12, 2026; Influenza A infections in the capital total 2,392, with H1N1 making nearly three-quarters of cases. Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda reviewed preparedness, including disease surveillance, laboratory testing, hospital capacity and treatment arrangements. H1N1 is a seasonal Influenza A subtype (swine flu) transmitted via respiratory droplets and contact with contaminated surfaces. Typical symptoms include fever, dry cough, sore throat, body aches, and fatigue; most recover in about a week, but higher case counts raise the risk of pneumonia or oxygen deprivation. A central review assessed surveillance (ILI/SARI), testing, bed and oxygen capacity, ventilators, and diagnostics; hospitals reported adequate staff and resources. Surveillance under Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme; vaccination remains important. Urgent care advised for low oxygen, breathing difficulty; antibiotics do not treat influenza.

article.articleHeadline: Antisipasi Kasus Zika di Bali, AS Beri Panduan 'Seks Aman' bagi Turis
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Anticipating Zika Cases in Bali, the U.S. Provides Safe-Sex Guidance for Tourists.
article.articleSummary: Zika Travel Health Notice Level 2 issued by the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for Bali, Indonesia, following rising reports of Zika in travelers returning from Bali. Zika virus is mosquito-borne; most infections are asymptomatic or mild, and there is no vaccine or specific antiviral treatment. The virus poses particular risk to pregnant women and those planning pregnancy, as infection during pregnancy can affect fetal development, especially in the first or second trimester, and the virus can also be sexually transmitted. The U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Indonesia reiterate prevention: use condoms or abstain from sex after travel. For men, abstinence or condom use is advised for 3 months after return; for women, 2 months. Travelers should follow these precautions to reduce Zika-related risks.

article.articleHeadline: Congo receives more than 16,000 doses of Ebola vaccine as it grapples with unprecedented outbreak
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa received 16,250 doses of Ervebo vaccine as part of a 70,000-dose allocation from the World Health Organization and partners, with more expected early next week. Dosas arrived at N'djili International Airport, Congo, amid the Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak—the fastest in history. The Bundibugyo strain currently has no approved treatment or vaccine, though Ervebo is licensed for Ebola and may offer some protection against Bundibugyo. As of Friday, the outbreak has 5,290 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths, and transmission is not yet peaked, potentially reaching three times the known rate and risking surpassing the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak that killed over 11,000. Containment is hampered by armed conflict, attacks on healthcare workers and facilities, mobile and displaced populations, and inadequate infrastructure.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo receives 16,000 doses of the Ebola vaccine - Al Ahly Stadium
article.articleSummary: On 22 August 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo received 16,250 doses of Merck’s Ervebo Ebola vaccine at Ndjili airport as it battles the seventh and deadliest outbreak in its history, first announced 15 May and likely spreading weeks earlier. The World Health Organization announced a total allocation of 70,000 Ervebo doses for DRC, with 20,000 for clinical trials and 50,000 for frontline health workers. The outbreak spans northern and eastern regions amid weak health infrastructure and armed conflict; current government data report 5,290 confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths. Ervebo is approved for Zaire ebolavirus, but its efficacy against Bundibugyo remains unconfirmed, though animal data hint some protection. WHO urges large-scale human trials; broader vaccine development continues, including Moderna’s mRNA vaccine, Oxford’s candidate, and Singapore’s Helman Labs advancing an rVSV Bundibugyo vaccine for human testing. Ebola has killed over 15,000 Africans in the past five decades.

article.articleHeadline: Living in fear, and not being paid: the health workers on the frontline of DRC's Ebola outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s north-eastern Ituri province has killed more than 2,500 people, with Bunia as the epicenter and Ituri reporting over 4,200 confirmed cases. The outbreak is the fastest-growing on record and is spreading across six of DRC’s 26 provinces; Uganda has reported 20 cases and two deaths in Kampala. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved treatments or vaccines, though trials are under way. Frontline health workers, including nurse Sophie Mwadawa Kabundo and hygiene worker Martin Bolombi at Bunia’s Elikya treatment centre, say wages since May have not been paid, with around 100 staff protesting a recent strike. Transmission occurs from wildlife to humans and between people via contact with infected body fluids; early symptoms include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, sore throat, progressing to vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, rash and kidney/liver impairment. Misinformation, mistrust and infrastructure deficits hinder response; WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern in May, and funding could run out within weeks in a region larger than France.

triage.headline_ja: 恐怖の中で働き、給料も払われない：DRCエボラアウトブレイクの最前線に立つ医療従事者たち
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最速拡大のエボラ流行が2500人以上の死者を出し、ウガンダへも越境拡大、WHOがPHEICを宣言済みでIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。

article.articleHeadline: Living in fear, and not being paid: the health workers on the frontline of DRC's Ebola outbreak - AOL
article.articleSummary: DRC is battling the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, centered in Ituri's north-east, with Bundibugyo virus. By 2026-08-22, the outbreak has more than 2,500 deaths and over 4,200 confirmed cases, spreading across six provinces and concentrated in Ituri near Uganda and South Sudan. Uganda has reported 20 cases and two deaths in Kampala. The WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern in May; sequencing indicates the outbreak began earlier, in February. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for Bundibugyo; trials are underway. Frontline workers at Bunia’s Elikya treatment centre report fear and unpaid wages—about 100 protested over bonuses; 160 healthcare workers have fallen ill, 43 have died. Transmission is via direct contact with blood or body fluids and contaminated surfaces, with symptoms from fever and fatigue to vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, rash, and organ impairment. Mistrust and misinformation hinder the response, including attacks on health facilities.

triage.headline_ja: 恐怖の中、給料も支払われず：DRCのエボラ流行の最前線に立つ医療従事者たち - AOL

triage.notes: ウガンダでも症例・死亡が報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないBundibugyoウイルスによる流行であり、医療従事者への未払い賃金や施設への攻撃など対応上の課題も深刻。

article.articleHeadline: 中國COVID-19疫情達高峰平台期 開始下降
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: China's COVID-19 outbreak has reached a peak plateau and is beginning to decline.
article.articleSummary: As of August 22, 2026, China's COVID-19 situation is reaching a peak plateau and beginning to decline. The China CDC reports that this year’s cases have been predominantly mild; the August early-to-mid peak plateau is easing, with declines more evident in the south. Overall epidemic intensity remains similar to the previous two years, and no variants detected to pose major public health risks, nor significant strain on healthcare services. The National Health Commission conveyed these findings at a seasonal climate and health briefing. In September, influenza vaccination will roll out nationwide as part of routine seasonality. The autumn–winter period is also when varicella, rhinovirus, norovirus, and enterovirus infections—including hand-foot-mouth disease—tend to rise, with schools identified as key sites for infection control.

triage.headline_ja: 中国のCOVID-19流行はピーク台地期に達し、下降し始めている
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のCOVID-19流行はピークを過ぎて下降傾向にあり、重症例増加や医療逼迫、変異株による公衆衛生上の重大リスクは報告されていないため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 中国国家衛生健康委員会による季節性報告であり、例年並みの流行規模で軽症が中心。今後の秋冬シーズンにおける水痘・ノロウイルス・エンテロウイルス等の流行動向は定期観察が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo erhalt mehr als 16.000 Impfdosen gegen Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kongo receives more than 16,000 Ebola vaccine doses.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo has received more than 16,000 doses of the Ebola vaccine Ervebo. The country is currently contending with its 17th Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization says the nation will receive a total of about 70,000 vaccine doses. The vaccine was developed against a different viral strain than that driving the present outbreak, so it will be tested first. Congolese authorities have reported roughly 5,300 confirmed infections and more than 2,500 deaths to date. The 17th outbreak is ongoing. No details on imported or exported cases are provided in this report.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴが16,000回分以上のエボラワクチンを受領
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で進行中の第17次エボラ流行は致死率が高く（確定感染5,300例中死亡2,500例超）、IHR基準の複数（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: WHOによるワクチン70,000回分の供給計画があり、国際的な支援体制がすでに動いている。ワクチンは現行流行株とは異なる株に対して開発されたものであり、有効性の検証が必要とされている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, negativi i test sul caso sospetto in Trentino VIDEO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, the tests are negative for the suspected case in Trentino VIDEO.
article.articleSummary: As of 22 August 2026, reports from Trentino state that tests on the biological samples of a man in isolation for a suspected Ebola case were negative. Diagnostic investigations conducted at Milan’s Sacco Hospital ruled out Ebola infection, confirming no contagion from this individual. The episode involved travel from the DRC and prompted health authorities in the region to respond to the suspected case, though laboratory results showed no infection. The report underscores the ongoing Ebola situation in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, but this case did not result in transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Swine Flu: Delhi Sees Rise In H1N1 Cases; Know Symptoms, How It Spreads And Prevention Tips
article.articleSummary: As of 22 August 2026, Delhi reports a rise in H1N1 swine flu cases. Common symptoms include fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches, joint and muscle pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, lethargy, loss of appetite and fatigue; some may experience cold-like symptoms, watery eyes and general weakness. H1N1 primarily spreads via respiratory droplets from coughing, sneezing or talking and can also transmit through contaminated surfaces, where the virus can persist for 24–48 hours. An infected person can spread the virus from about one day before symptoms appear to roughly five to seven days after illness onset. Monsoon conditions may elevate seasonal influenza activity; vulnerable individuals should take extra precautions. H1N1 is treatable and most cases are mild; preventive home measures include regular handwashing, covering coughs/sneezes, avoiding close contact, and staying home when sick.

article.articleHeadline: 16,250 Ebola Vaccine Doses Arrive in DRC as Outbreak Kills 2,516
article.articleSummary: 16,250 doses of the Ervebo Ebola vaccine arrived in Kinshasa, DRC, as the country battles its deadliest outbreak, with 2,516 deaths. The shipment is part of 70,000 doses made available by the World Health Organization, of which 50,000 will go to frontline and health workers and 20,000 will be used in a clinical trial. The outbreak, declared on May 15, has produced 5,290 confirmed cases and is rapidly spreading across northern and eastern DRC where healthcare access is limited. Ervebo targets the Zaire strain, but the ongoing outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain; WHO experts are studying whether Ervebo can confer protection, with early animal studies showing some potential. The WHO has recommended a large-scale human trial of Ervebo, with two other Bundibugyo-targeting vaccines in clinical trials.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Swine Flu Cases in Delhi: Rising H1N1 Threat in Delhi! 1,777 cases reported, learn the symptoms and preventive measures - CNBC Awaaz
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-22, Delhi reports 2,392 Influenza A cases this year, with 1,777 confirmed H1N1 infections (Swine Flu). H1N1 spreads mainly via respiratory droplets from coughs and sneezes and via contaminated surfaces. Incubation is 3–5 days; symptoms resemble seasonal flu. In children, warning signs include breathing difficulty, dehydration, fever with rash, lethargy, and confusion; seek medical care promptly. Diagnosis may involve clinical assessment and laboratory testing to identify influenza A subtypes. Most healthy individuals recover with rest, fluids, and over-the-counter analgesics; antivirals such as oseltamivir and zanamivir can shorten illness if started early, especially in severe cases. Prevention emphasizes hand hygiene, covering coughs/sneezes, not touching the face, avoiding close contact with the sick, staying home when ill, and not sharing personal items.

article.articleSummary: DR Congo battles its deadliest Ebola outbreak across northern and eastern regions; it received 16,000 doses of Merck’s Ebola vaccine Ervebo, with Ndjili International Airport in Kinshasa reporting 16,250 doses on Friday as the country confronts the outbreak. article.articleHeadline: Конгода Эбола өршіді: БҰҰ індетке қарсы қаржы бірнеше аптаға ғана жететінін ескертті
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Surges in Congo: The UN Warned That Funding to Fight the Outbreak Would Last Only a Few Weeks
article.articleSummary: Ebola surges in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as the UN warns funding to fight the outbreak would last only a few weeks. Since the outbreak was declared on May 15, 2026, there have been 5,290 Ebola cases and 2,516 deaths; about 1,152 recoveries and roughly 840 still isolated or hospitalized. The case fatality rate stands at 47.6%. The outbreak now spans Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Upper Uele, Chopo and Lower Uele. Health workers remain at high risk: 160 infections, 43 deaths. Attacks on ambulances and health facilities by armed groups and locals hinder response; emergency vehicles and clinics have been attacked or burned. Basic social and governmental services are lacking; banking is largely non-operational in eastern provinces, affecting salary payments to responders. Two years of funding cuts have reduced humanitarian capacity by more than 30%, but the UN and Congolese authorities persist in containment efforts.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラが急拡大：国連は対策資金があと数週間しか持たないと警告
triage.triage_reason: 致死率47.6%の大規模エボラ流行が複数州に拡大し、資金・医療体制の逼迫と武装勢力による攻撃で対応が困難化しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 5,290症例・2,516死亡、致死率47.6%と極めて深刻。医療従事者感染160件・死亡43件、武装勢力による医療施設・救急車攻撃、資金不足により人道支援能力が30%以上低下している点が重大な懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Medicamento oferecido no SUS reduz casos de malária no Brasil
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Drug offered by Brazil's SUS reduces malaria cases in Brazil
article.articleSummary: Brazil’s 2025 malaria data show deaths down to 39 (from 56 in 2024) and severe malaria reduced about 30%, with 118,037 national cases—a 15% drop and the lowest since 1978. Gains come with tafenoquine in the SUS (single-dose) for adults (≥16 years, weight ≥35 kg), and a March 2026 pediatric formulation for ages 2+ years and ≥10 kg; by June 2026, over 33,700 people were treated, including 3,920 in Indigenous health districts (DSEIs). In 2025, malaria reductions surpassed 40% in Indigenous territories and Amazonian rural settlements; Yanomami territory treated cases (1,515) and relapse rates fell sharply by early 2026. Jan–Jul malaria cases dropped 55% (17,000 to 7,600). Measles saw 38 imported cases in São Paulo, Espírito Santo, Rio de Janeiro and Tocantins; vaccination reinforcement preserved Brazil’s measles-free status in 2025, with campaigns vaccinating tens of thousands in cities like São Paulo.

article.articleSummary: On 2026-08-22, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Health Ministry announced the arrival of the first Ebola vaccine batch to fight the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak, with 16,520 doses delivered to Kinshasa on Friday and more than 50,000 additional doses expected in the coming days. There are no vaccines or specific therapies licensed for Bundibugyo ebolavirus yet. Early lab and animal data suggest vaccines approved for Zaire ebolavirus may offer some protection against Bundibugyo. The World Health Organization has allocated 70,000 doses of Zaire ebolavirus vaccine to the DRC: 20,000 for a phase 3 trial to assess protection against Bundibugyo, and 50,000 for frontline health workers. The rollout signals vaccination and clinical-trial efforts as authorities respond to the outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: 逾1.6万剂伊波拉疫苗运抵民主刚果
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 16,000 doses of the Ebola vaccine have arrived in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: More than 16,000 doses of Merck’s Ervebo Ebola vaccine arrived in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) last night as the country fights its deadliest Ebola outbreak to date. The outbreak, declared May 15 as the 17th Ebola event in the DRC, has likely been spreading for weeks, with thousands of deaths concentrated in northern and eastern regions amid weak control and scarce health infrastructure and longstanding armed-group activity. The World Health Organization (WHO) announced a total allocation of 70,000 Ervebo doses for the country: 20,000 for clinical trials and 50,000 prioritized for frontline healthcare workers. Ervebo targets Zaire ebolavirus, but its effectiveness against Bundibugyo ebolavirus—currently circulating in DRC—remains unconfirmed, though preliminary animal data suggest some protection. As of the latest figures, the outbreak has 5,290 laboratory-confirmed cases and 2,516 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: 1.6万回分以上のエボラワクチンがコンゴ民主共和国に到着
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最悪規模とされるエボラ流行が継続しており、5,290例の確定症例と2,516人の死亡が報告されている。武力紛争や脆弱な保健インフラも相まって国際的懸念が高く、IHR・WPRO双方の基準を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 本流行はDRCで宣言された第17次エボラ流行であり、ザイール株用ワクチンEervebo（Merck製）が現地で流行中のブンディブギョ株にどの程度有効かは未確認。武装勢力の活動により対応が困難化しており、国際的な支援（WHOによるワクチン配分）が既に行われている。
